doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: Old Man Solace's grocery, the little hall and the Catholic church on Patterson Street
summary: Asked about parks and lawn parties, Martin describes a small place at old man Solace's grocery on Patterson Street, with stables and a church next door, where people danced.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Are there any other parks over there that you can think of? Or did they have many lawn parties? Fish fries. Fish fries. Fish fries. Any special places they'd have that or just any home or wherever they...

Well, you take... They used to have a little place, Old Man Solace there. Oh, that's at the Cudolph, isn't it? No. Right there in the Lisey. That's where that's the Lisey there, yeah. Old Man Solace. Yeah, well... They all used to play that. Yeah, that's where Little Hall was. Little Hall. When you started the church, they had the Catholic Church in it. Not that.
Not that. But you mean cross by all the other...
Right across where Sigacy. Sigacy, yeah. Old Man Solace had that grocery there. Yeah, I don't know. The stables was right in the back of it.

Now, where Old Man John of Conjean, they used to cut the pigeon wing that was there by Frank Theod. Right next to the grocery unit, they had that little hole there and the church was next to it. The Catholic Church was next to it.
The Catholic Church was next to it.

Is there yet, you told me? The Catholic Church where... Where... Where... Where... Where Old Man Solace used to be. What street was that about? What street? That's down on Patterson Street. Right up to Levy down there on Patterson. That's years ago. I was a boy then, you know. I was a boy then, you know.
I was a boy then, you know. Oh, wait a minute. I was a boy then, you know. You know, you know. Oh, wait a minute. That's a long time.
